deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the earlier pages. X is a topological space and I an ordered set. (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of subspaces satisfying the conditions a), b) of (1'), which are presumably: each X_i is closed, and i ≤ j implies X_i ⊂ X_j. The 'flag spaces' are
X_{Δ_r} = {(x, i_0 ≤ … ≤ i_r) : x ∈ X_{i_0}} ⊂ X × I_{Δ_r},
where I_{Δ_r} is the set of r-simplices of the nerve of I. So X_{Δ_0} = ⊔_i X_i and X_{Δ_1} = ⊔_{i≤j} X_i. Together they form a simplicial space, or a semi-simplicial space if only non-degenerate flags (strictly increasing chains) are kept.

Problem. The previous page asks to recover X from X_{Δ_*}. This page adds two conditions:
- c) X = ∪ X_i;
- d) X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k≤i, k≤j} X_k.

These make X the colimit (coequalizer) of X_{Δ_1} ⇉ X_{Δ_0}. Hence X is also the colimit of the whole (semi-)simplicial diagram, since the colimit of a simplicial object only involves degrees 0 and 1.

Set-theoretic argument:
- c) makes ⊔X_i → X surjective.
- Suppose (x,i) and (x,j) have the same image. By d) there is k ≤ i, j with x ∈ X_k. Then (x,k) ∈ X_{Δ_1} maps to (x,i) and to (x,j), so the two points are identified by a zigzag of length 2.
- Hence the fibres of ⊔X_i → X are exactly the classes of the equivalence relation generated by X_{Δ_1}.

Topologically, X carries the quotient topology because the X_i are closed, provided the closed cover is finite or locally finite. The next page does in fact assume I finite.

Proposition (22): the canonical map lim→ X_{Δ_*} → X is a homeomorphism. Grothendieck notes it holds for both variants, all flags and non-degenerate flags.

Corollary, begun here and continued on the next page. It reverses the construction. Start from a 'topological ordered space' (X_{Δ_0}, X_{Δ_1} ⊂ X_{Δ_0}×X_{Δ_0}), i.e. an internal poset in Top. Assume X_{Δ_0} has a partition (X_i) into clopen pieces, and that each Γ_{ij} = X_{Δ_1} ∩ (X_i×X_j) is either empty or the graph of a closed immersion X_i → X_j. Then:
- such data are the same as an I-indexed inductive system of spaces with closed-immersion transition maps;
- if I is finite with binary infima, X = lim→ X_i, recovered as the quotient of X_{Δ_0} by X_{Δ_1}.

Purpose in the 'topos stratifié' project. The stratification of X by closed subsets indexed by a poset is encoded as a simplicial space or internal poset. Conditions c) and d) say every point has a well-defined minimal index (for finite I). Equivalently, there is a continuous map X → I with the Alexandrov topology, i.e. a poset-stratified space, and X is glued from its closed strata-closures.
errors: Formula (20) on the previous page is written as a pushout X_{Δ_0} ⊔_{X_{Δ_1}} X_{Δ_0} of the span a, b. What is really meant, and what (22) states, is the coequalizer of a, b : X_{Δ_1} ⇉ X_{Δ_0}. The literal pushout of two copies of X_{Δ_0} would not give X. This is a notational slip.

Gap: for the map to be a homeomorphism rather than just a continuous bijection, one needs ⊔X_i → X to be a quotient map. With the X_i closed this holds if the cover is finite or locally finite, or if X carries the weak topology determined by the X_i. For arbitrary infinite I, conditions a)–d) do not suffice. The next page silently restricts to finite I.
Condition d) contains an elided clause ('…'), presumably a restriction such as i, j incomparable. As written for all (i,j) it is still harmless.

ideas.what: Encoding a closed cover/filtration indexed by a poset as a (semi-)simplicial 'flag space' X_{Δ_r} ⊂ X × N_r(I)
ideas.modern_name: Čech-type nerve of a poset-indexed closed cover; simplicial space associated to a diagram (Bousfield–Kan/Segal style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968, classifying spaces and spectral sequences), Bousfield–Kan (1972)

ideas.what: X is the colimit of its closed pieces when the cover is closed under intersections up to unions (condition d)
ideas.modern_name: Closed covers as colimits; gluing lemma / closed descent for finite closed covers

ideas.what: Topological ordered space (X_0, X_1 ⊂ X_0×X_0) with a clopen partition whose pieces are linked by closed immersions is equivalent to an inductive system of spaces indexed by a poset
ideas.modern_name: Internal posets/categories in Top; diagram ↔ Grothendieck construction (category of elements) in a topological setting

ideas.what: Conditions c) and d) amount to each point having a minimal index, i.e. a continuous map X → I (Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A (2010s); earlier MacPherson/Treumann exit-path literature

missed.claim: In 1981 Grothendieck encodes a stratification by a poset of closed subspaces as a simplicial 'flag space' over the nerve of I, or as a topological ordered space, and reconstructs X as its colimit. This anticipates the now-standard treatment of stratified spaces as spaces over a poset, and of stratified objects via simplicial or internal-poset data, as in exit-path ∞-categories and Lurie's poset-stratified spaces. The mathematics itself is elementary.
missed.quote: l'application canonique (22) lim→ X_{Δ_*} →~ X est un homéomorphisme
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents an early formulation of poset-stratified spaces within the 'topos stratifié' programme. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is an elementary gluing statement: a space is the coequalizer of its closed cover's flag space under an intersection condition. Its only interest is the stratified-topos framing, which foreshadows poset-stratified spaces.
transcription_corrections: The insertion over the crossed-out 'on devrait appeler au dire' should read '(c'est équivalent)'. The phrase is then '…qui assurent trivialement la relation (20), (c'est équivalent), de façon "formelle":'.

'pour les deux variantes (drapeaux quelconques, drapeaux non dégénérés) pour les espaces de drapeaux X_{Δ_r}'. The word 'dimensions' in the machine transcription is a misreading of the crossed-out 'drapeaux'.

The last lines read approximately 'X_{Δ_0} b) un des parties à la fois ouvertes et fermées'. The intended sense, confirmed by the next page, is a partition (X_i)_{i∈I} of X_{Δ_0} into parts that are both open and closed.
In (22) the diagram should show face maps X_{Δ_0} ⇇ X_{Δ_1} ⇚ X_{Δ_2} …, i.e. a simplicial space.
